trial.ground_truth: Payment delays 3 seconds while caller timeout is 2 seconds
trial.predicted_root_cause: Failing trace 1feb060fcd91440def2fe8f112df0716 shows the gateway's client span POST http://order-service:8000/checkout with duration_us=2005324 (~2005ms) and otel.status_description \"ReadTimeout:\" → HTTP 502. In the same trace, downstream calls complete in microseconds/milliseconds (payment POST /charge ~35us, user SELECT ~24us, inventory GET ~243us), so no downstream service or shared pool is the source. Order-service /checkout error logs all show near-identical ~2018ms durations with status 502 — a fixed injected delay — and pg_stat_statements records SELECT pg_sleep($1) with mean_exec_time ~1202ms over 531 calls, an active delay-injection primitive. The delay sits inside order-service's request path; gateway's ReadTimeout converts the slow call into 502s, so gateway's 502s are derived, not independent.

regression_risks: Raising the gateway read timeout to SLO could mask a recurring slow checkout/DB path and remove the circuit-breaker protection that currently bounds failure, increasing load on an already-strained order-service during real faults
No code patch means the injected fault (if external) will recur on re-injection; operational remediation is not durable
Cumulative/cumulative Redis and pool counters (E-feddf98460614f89, cumulative note) may mislead if not snapshot-diffed; treating them as point-in-time could cause false clean readings
critic_result.test_sufficiency: Insufficient for unique root-cause attribution. The before/after experiment shows recovery, but the operator-runner causality limit is explicitly stated (not an AI repair, not a unique mechanism). No test isolates the injection site: pg_sleep is not tied to order-service, the fault key was never observed set, and no clean-trace-plus-injected-trace A/B was performed. Patch scope search empty, so no regression test applies.
critic_result.verification_summary:
Diagnosis of order-service /checkout as the stall site is well-supported: order-service logs show consistent ~2018ms 502s (E-32932f9e84944528), gateway emits matching 502s with shared trace IDs (E-05ff293c377d4933), and the failing trace (E-2c69efaf86e84764) shows the gateway→order client span at ~2005ms with ReadTimeout while child spans to payment/user/inventory are sub-ms. Before/after windows are consistent (E-b4cb1428b1794b41 before: order 2018ms/100% err, payment 3006ms; E-d4d59ae9703444f6 after: order 29ms/0% err, payment 5ms), and the after window is clean across all services. The pg_sleep signature (mean ~1202ms) is a plausible injected primitive.

However, the specific claim "injected ~2s delay in order-service's OWN request path" is not uniquely established. Note: (a) the pg_sleep statement was never attributed to order-service application_name — the observed activity for order-service shows only SELECT 1 and INSERT INTO orders (E-8f98b51038f74fbe), so the delay could be in a shared DB proxy/service, and (b) payment-service shows 3006ms p50 in the before window but fast in after — the sub-ms child spans in the failing trace do not alone prove payment is purely a symptom vs. an unrelated concurrent cause. The evidence supports order-service as the bottleneck, but the exact injection site (handler code vs. DB layer vs. shared dependency) remains unconfirmed, and the fault key harness (E-d7c5ca01beaa45c7) is only a code fact, not an observed set key. Repository search (E-53519bd2d6ad4c40) confirms no patch scope match, consistent with NO_CODE_PATCH.

Gateway read timeout (~2s) may itself be a primary fault (misconfigured/low client timeout) turning a normally ~1.2s checkout into 502s, making the 'injection' only partially the cause

judgment.explanation: The submission's category (DOWNSTREAM_TIMEOUT) and its identification of the mechanism (a ~2s injected delay causing the caller's ReadTimeout and 502) are partially right, but it places the root cause in the wrong service. Ground truth: the affected service is payment-service, whose processing is delayed 3 seconds while the caller's (order-service) timeout is 2 seconds. The observed metrics support this: payment-service shows ~3006ms latency while all others are at most ~2s, meaning the delay is in payment-service and order-service hits its ReadTimeout waiting on payment. The submission instead claims the delay lives inside order-service's own request path and treats payment-service's latency as a fast child span/symptom, directly contradicting the immutable ground truth (payment delay > caller timeout). Because the mechanism is attributed to the wrong service, the causal chain is materially incorrect, even though it correctly observed the downstream-timeout pattern and 502s. Evidence quality is 2: multiple independent supporting observations (failing trace, paired gateway/order-service logs with matched trace IDs, latency metrics showing payment-service at ~3s).

initial_hypotheses: order-service is the primary fault domain: its 95.65% error rate on POST /checkout propagates upstream to gateway (502s), while its downstream dependencies postgres/inventory-service remain healthy.
payment-service latency (~3s on POST /charge) acts as a downstream backpressure/blocking dependency for order-service, causing checkout timeouts rather than payment errors.
A shared infrastructure dependency (redis connection pool, postgres connection pool, or redpanda backlog delaying notification-service) is degrading order-service's nested calls.
gateway errors are secondary/derived from order-service failures, not an independent fault, given gateway's downstream order-service path is the only error-producing branch.

decision.hypothesis: order-service /checkout is stalled by an injected ~2s delay in its own request path; gateway's httpx client to order-service hits a ~2s ReadTimeout and returns 502. Downstream deps (payment/inventory/user) are fast, so this is a delay injected at order-service, not downstream backpressure.
decision.root_cause: Failing trace 1feb060fcd91440def2fe8f112df0716 shows the gateway's client span POST http://order-service:8000/checkout with duration_us=2005324 (~2005ms) and otel.status_description \"ReadTimeout:\" → HTTP 502. In the same trace, downstream calls complete in microseconds/milliseconds (payment POST /charge ~35us, user SELECT ~24us, inventory GET ~243us), so no downstream service or shared pool is the source. Order-service /checkout error logs all show near-identical ~2018ms durations with status 502 — a fixed injected delay — and pg_stat_statements records SELECT pg_sleep($1) with mean_exec_time ~1202ms over 531 calls, an active delay-injection primitive. The delay sits inside order-service's request path; gateway's ReadTimeout converts the slow call into 502s, so gateway's 502s are derived, not independent.
llm_findings: Failing trace 1feb060fcd91440def2fe8f112df0716: gateway client span POST http://order-service:8000/checkout = ~2005ms with otel.status_description 'ReadTimeout:', returning 502.
Same failing trace: payment POST /charge ~35us, user SELECT ~24us, inventory GET ~243us — downstream services are healthy, excluding downstream backpressure as the source.
order-service /checkout error logs are uniformly ~2018ms with status 502, indicating a fixed injected delay rather than variable load.
pg_stat_statements shows SELECT pg_sleep($1) mean_exec_time ~1202ms (531 calls) — an active delay-injection primitive consistent with the stall.
gateway 502s and order-service 502s share trace IDs, confirming gateway errors are derived from order-service failures.
payment-service's elevated latency is a downstream symptom within the delayed checkout path, not the root cause; sampled healthy trace and aggregate metrics are consistent, not conflicting.
decision.recommended_fix: Operationally: (1) Inspect and clear the injected delay in order-service — check the Redis fault key ('fault:'+name, services/runtime.py:40-41) and any pg_sleep delay call in order-service's checkout path; removing the injected fault restores health. (2) As immediate mitigation, gateway's httpx client read timeout (~2s) is shorter than the injected delay, so raise the client timeout toward the service SLO or add circuit-breaker/backoff to avoid hard 502s. (3) Alert on order-service /checkout p95 latency and gateway 502 ratio, and on pg_stat_statements for unintended long-running sleep queries. No source patch is applicable because the defective delay lives outside the allowlisted patch scope (services/pricing.py, services/runtime.py, tests/pricing_contract.py).
decision.reasoning_summary: Three independent sources converge: (1) order-service and gateway error logs both list /checkout 502s at ~2018ms in the same window, sharing trace IDs (E-32932f9e84944528, E-05ff293c377d4933); (2) raw failing trace shows the gateway→order-service client span timing out at ~2005ms with otel.status_description \"ReadTimeout:\", while payment/user/inventory child spans in the same trace are sub-millisecond (E-2c69efaf86e84764); (3) pg_stat_statements shows SELECT pg_sleep($1) mean_exec_time ~1202ms across 531 calls (E-8f98b51038f74fbe). Delayed order-service checkout → gateway read timeout → 502. Payment-service's elevated latency is within the delayed checkout path (its child spans are fast in the failing trace), so it is a symptom, not the origin. The sampled healthy trace (E-9c6fbdf5ac794e7a) and cumulative/aggregate metrics (E-1b183d2970224fee) are consistent but not independently decisive; they do not contradict the failing-trace mechanism. Residual uncertainty is the exact delay site inside order-service, whose app code is outside the allowlisted patch scope.

deterministic_signals.explanation: Gateway 50% 502s are the front door of order-service /checkout failures: gateway error logs show /checkout 502 at ~2015ms, and the failing trace shows gateway's client span to order-service timing out with ReadTimeout. Gateway errors are derived from order-service, not independent.
order-service 95.65% error rate on /checkout at a uniform ~2018ms is the primary fault; pg_stat_statements shows pg_sleep($1) mean_exec_time ~1202ms, indicating an injected delay in its request path.

payment-service is not the origin. In the failing trace, payment's POST /charge child span completes in ~35us and its DB INSERT in ~28us; payment latency appears only as an invoked dependency within order-service's already-delayed checkout, so it is a symptom, not the causal fault.

remaining_uncertainty: Exact location of the injected delay inside order-service (handler vs. its DB/pricing call) is not visible; order-service app code is outside read scope.
The ~2s figure is bounded by the gateway client read timeout, not necessarily the full injected sleep (pg_sleep mean ~1202ms).
Whether the fault key is set on order-service specifically vs. a shared dependency cannot be confirmed without the fault harness.
